## Purpose and scope

This protocol measures the purity of DNA extracts and PCR products with the NanoDrop One: the absorbance ratios A~260~/A~280~ and A~260~/A~230~. It is used on extracts from EnGeL-MOLB-DNA-MAG, -DNA-COL, -DNA-BARC and -DNA-BEE, and on RNA from EnGeL-MOLB-RNA. NanoDrop concentrations are not used for DNA amounts: for those use fluorometry (EnGeL-MOLB-QUBIT for single samples, EnGeL-MOLB-PICOGREEN for 96-well plates).

## Principle

The spectrophotometer measures the absorbance of a 1.5 µL drop at 230, 260 and 280 nm. Nucleic acids absorb most at 260 nm, proteins at 280 nm, and salts, phenol, guanidine and carbohydrates around 230 nm, so the ratios show carry-over from the extraction. The absorbance at 260 nm also includes RNA, single-stranded DNA and free nucleotides, which is why NanoDrop concentrations overestimate double-stranded DNA.

## Reagent preparation

Not applicable.

## Procedure

### Before starting

- Use filter tips.
- Mix each sample gently and spin it down before measuring.

### Measurement

(@) Turn on the NanoDrop and let the initialisation run normally.
(@) Clean the pedestal with 7 µL nuclease-free water.
(@) Select the program for the sample type (dsDNA for DNA extracts and PCR products; RNA for RNA).
(@) Load 1.5 µL of blank (the last reagent used in the extraction protocol), close the arm to measure it, then wipe the pedestal.
(@) Load 1.5 µL of sample, close the arm to measure it, then wipe the pedestal. Repeat for each sample.
(@) After all measurements, clean the pedestal with 7 µL nuclease-free water.

### After finishing

{{< include ../../includes/_before-you-leave.qmd >}}

## Calculations

Not applicable: the instrument reports the ratios and the concentration (ng/µL).

## Quality control

| Control | Purpose | Acceptance criterion |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Blank | Zero on the sample matrix | Measured before the samples, with the buffer the samples are in |
| DNA purity (A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~) | Protein, salt or organic carry-over | Ideal: A~260~/A~280~ 1.8–2.0 and A~260~/A~230~ 2.0–2.2. Values outside are flagged, not failed: the PCR decides |
| Extraction blanks | Contamination during extraction | < 5 ng/µL (regarded as noise); also no band after PCR (extraction protocols) |
| RNA purity | Carry-over in RNA extracts | [TO CONFIRM: ranges for RNA] |

## Data and metadata

- **Outputs:** A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~ and the NanoDrop concentration (ng/µL) for each sample.
- **Where:** the *Sample_Tracking* sheet of the Metabarcoding Lab Pipeline workbook (A260/280, A260/230) or the project's records, and the lab book; instrument use in the NanoDrop logbook.

::: {.callout-note title="Minimum to record"}
- EnGeL sample label; date; operator
- Program used (dsDNA or RNA) and the blank
- A~260~/A~280~, A~260~/A~230~ and the concentration, marked as NanoDrop values
:::

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Solution |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Reading unstable or ratios odd | Dirty pedestal or bubble in the drop | Clean the pedestal with nuclease-free water; load the drop again without bubbles. |
| Low A~260~/A~230~ in all samples | Wrong blank, or carry-over of extraction buffers | Blank with the buffer the samples are in; check the wash steps of the extraction. |
| Concentration much higher than by fluorometry | RNA, single-stranded DNA or nucleotides | Expected: use Qubit or PicoGreen for DNA amounts. |

## Remarks

For DNA amounts (library preparation, normalisation) always use fluorometry; NanoDrop is for purity.
